faultEvidence: One hundred concurrent settlement requests share one stalled sweep; durable completion resolves before that remote dependency.
One failed settlement stops the batch; repeated triggers during backoff make no further dependency calls. Successful batches drain no more than eight retained leases.
An acquired-but-unbound lease retains its original identity and fences new admission until settled.
Sixteen same-owner stalled submissions admit eight lookups; excess calls are rejected, while another owner and original-owner recovery lookup retain separate admission.
A pre-exhaustion sibling success after the deadline does not reopen full capacity; a real post-cooldown probe does.
Transient failure cooldown survives restored engine state.
One hundred early Continue calls after restoration make no model request or step/reservation change; Retry-After remains a lower bound.
Two configured tool workers never exceed that count; failed persistence stops queued starts and retains both in-flight results.
correctedFixtureFailures: Two JSON/SSE continuation integration tests initially resumed before the new retained deadline. They now assert the wait and advance only the synthetic clock before continuation; all 60 tests pass.
limits: No real provider generation, induced real quota exhaustion, production traffic benchmark or public application cutover.
Runtime images are installed locally; SDK/client application publication and authenticated checkpoint-store integration remain separate.
Process-local request and per-batch tool limits do not provide distributed tenant fairness, RPS control or aggregate downstream concurrency guarantees.
Observation and submission allowances share the existing database pool; a database outage can deny both.
Caller-owned callbacks and persistence still require their own domain deadlines, access control and idempotency.
Unknown writes/side effects remain subject to reconciliation; no automatic replay or exactly-once guarantee.
Both execution gates remain closed. Premium retains one paused connected account; Standard has none.
No schema, permission, credential, account or quota-counter change in this pass. Existing schema contract inspected read-only; installed boundary checks retain that authority.
The local build scan checks selected markers and runtime traces, not all possible data disclosure or the live public site.
No new graphical chat UI, visual score or browser acceptance.

The engine initiates terminal persistence asynchronously from its lifecycle event. Completed stream delivery does not prove terminal-write or lease-settlement commit; failed writes continue to block new admission.
